clue.text: Warming the middle of the building? All of it

definitions.text: Warming the middle of the building? All of it

blocks.clueFragment: Warming the middle of the building?
blocks.note: surface reading: heating only the core of a building
setter's reading: the system that warms the whole building from one central source

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether only the middle of a building gets warm, then insists the whole place does.
explanation.walkthrough: The question tempts you to read 'central' literally as 'in the middle'; the tag 'All of it' reminds you that the household system warms every room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a domestic system where one boiler or furnace sends warmth through pipes to every room of a house.

clue.text: Levy on the overweight?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fat tax charged on heavy people
setter's reading: a tax charged on company profits, with 'corporation' also an old jokey word for a pot belly

explanation.surface: A government proposes a tax on people who weigh too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old British humorous word for a large paunch, so the business tax doubles as a tax on big bellies.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies in Britain pay this charge on their profits, and the paunch sense of its first word makes it a fat levy.

clue.text: Worn strip

blocks.note: surface reading: a frayed or threadbare strip of something
setter's reading: a strip of fabric that is worn around the collar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' looks like 'shabby', but here it means 'put on and carried on the body', so the strip is a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a long narrow band of cloth knotted at the collar and hung down the shirt front.

clue.text: Making it another time just for fun

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., building something again
second meaning: leisure activity done for enjoyment

explanation.surface: Someone remakes a thing purely for the pleasure of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word as re-creation for the first meaning; the second is the ordinary word for pastimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbies and pastimes pursued for enjoyment count as recreation, while re-creation literally means producing something again.

clue.text: Future made up ground

blocks.note: surface reading: land built up for later use
setter's reading: the lost distance one must make up, from the idiom about making up lost ground

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to make up leeway' means to recover lost ground; the leeway is the margin still to be made up in future.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is sideways drift of a ship off course, and so lost ground or a margin of time left to recover.

clue.text: Late-duty journalist was praised highly

definitions.note: the answer is the past tense 'praised highly'; 'was' is part of the definition as a passive reading, so read it as 'praised highly'

blocks.note: late means former, as in an ex-partner
a toll is a charge or levy, a kind of duty
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter who worked the night shift was lavishly complimented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late-duty journalist' reads as a night-shift reporter, but it splits into three words that each give a short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, so someone who was extolled received lavish compliments.

clue.text: Fellow to include ambassador

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A man is asked to bring an envoy into the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is not a link word here but the outer letters; HE goes inside it to give THEO. Crossword setters often define a man's name simply as 'fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theo is a male first name, and setters use a general word for a man to stand for any boy's name.

clue.text: Ran up with speed to provide commentary

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
rate is pace or speed

explanation.surface: A commentator dashes up quickly to give the commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator describes events to listeners as they happen, which is to narrate them.

clue.text: By a circuitous route through the estate

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for going a long way about, or talking in circles
second meaning: a literal walk past every home on a housing estate

explanation.surface: Someone takes the long way, weaving between the houses of a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means taking an unnecessarily long route; the estate here is a housing estate, so the phrase is also literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a needlessly roundabout journey or way of speaking, and is literally a walk around homes.

clue.text: Use again on another bike?

blocks.note: first meaning: to process waste so it can be used again
second meaning: to ride a bicycle once more

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading, splitting the word into 're-' and 'cycle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprocessing bottles, paper and other waste so the material serves a fresh purpose is the everyday meaning.

clue.text: The boor performed on this lute

indicators.note: performed suggests something worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncouth man played a tune on this stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorbo is a large bass member of the lute family, with extra long-necked strings, used in Baroque music.

clue.text: Put forward for discussion at a meeting being above-board

definitions.text: Put forward for discussion at a meeting

blocks.clueFragment: Put forward for discussion at a meeting
blocks.note: first meaning: a proposal laid before a committee
second meaning: open and honest, like cards laid face up

explanation.surface: A proposal raised at a meeting is entirely open and honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion placed before a committee is tabled, and openly displayed dealings are like cards shown face up.

clue.text: Early bird?

blocks.note: surface reading: the proverbial person who gets up early
setter's reading: bird is British slang for a young woman, here one whose first name means daybreak

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a woman, and a woman's name that is also the earliest part of the day makes her an 'early' bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak, the first light of morning, is also a common girl's name, so she is the earliest of women.

clue.text: Did it illuminate the Ark?

blocks.note: surface reading: asking what lit Noah's vessel
setter's reading: a powerful lamp, whose name joins Noah's deluge and a light

explanation.walkthrough: Noah's Ark floated on the Flood, so a lamp shining during the Flood gives the name of a powerful outdoor lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadiums and building fronts are lit by broad, powerful lamps, and the name splits into the Biblical deluge plus a lamp.

clue.text: A match for some holy scriptures

blocks.note: taken as written
a vesta is a short wooden or wax match

explanation.surface: Someone offers a match, as if to light up a sacred text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A match for' looks like 'an equal to', but 'match' is the thing you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the collection of sacred texts of Zoroastrianism, the ancient Persian religion.

clue.text: Determined to be infernally crooked?

blocks.note: the inferno is hell
bent means crooked, both in shape and in the sense of dishonest

explanation.surface: Someone resolved on being wicked, crooked in the devilish way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hell-bent on something means being recklessly resolved to do it whatever the cost.

clue.text: Continued to be left behind

blocks.note: first meaning: stayed in the same state
second meaning: stayed put after others had gone

explanation.surface: Someone kept on being abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both persisting in a state and staying in a place once everyone else has departed.

clue.text: Got better when I am put to the test

blocks.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
to prove something is to test it, as in a proving ground

explanation.surface: Someone claims they perform better whenever they are tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who got better made progress, recovered or grew more skilled than before.

clue.text: A crop I'd cultivated for chap with a lance

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over and worked, so the letters are dug up and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer grew a crop for a man who carries a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bullfight the mounted man who jabs the bull with a long spear is the picador.

clue.text: Hesitate, injuring leg behind marsh

indicators.note: an injured limb is twisted out of shape, so its letters are scrambled
behind says the second piece comes after the first in the answer

blocks.note: a bog is a marsh
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from crossing a marsh for fear of hurting a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To boggle at something is to shy away or balk at it, holding back in doubt or alarm.

clue.text: Go left to Iowa taking collection of nerve cells

definitions.note: the answer is plural, the definition singular

blocks.note: gang is an old Scots and northern word for go
L is the abbreviation for left
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A traveller heads off to Iowa and picks up a bundle of nerve tissue on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Gang for go survives in Scots, apt in a Scotsman puzzle. The definition is singular though the answer is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a clump of neuron bodies outside the brain; ganglia is its plural.

clue.text: Happen to be a season in America

blocks.note: taken as written
fall is the American name for autumn

explanation.surface: Something occurs in the autumn on the far side of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: When misfortune befalls someone it happens to them, usually something bad.

clue.text: Devilish cut?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, Old Nick, the devil

blocks.note: first meaning: Old ..., a name for the Devil
second meaning: a small notch or wound

explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a traditional English nickname for Satan; the second meaning is a small cut, as in shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the old nickname of Satan and a shallow notch or small wound from a blade.

clue.text: Papal treasurer exchanged longer mace

indicators.note: things exchanged are swapped about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Pope's money man swapped his ceremonial staff for a longer one.
explanation.definitionFit: The camerlengo is the cardinal who runs the Vatican's finances and property and governs during a papal vacancy.

clue.text: Reptile had many an old bird

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
the roc is the giant bird of old Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A reptile once owned plenty of ancient birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The short informal name for a crocodile, the large armoured reptile of rivers.

clue.text: And even a firedog

blocks.note: taken as written
to iron something is to make it smooth and even

explanation.surface: A list adds even one more item: a firedog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like an adverb ('even a firedog') but is a verb, to smooth flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedogs are a pair of metal stands that support logs in an open hearth, also called andirons.

clue.text: Bell brought by messenger to America

blocks.note: angel comes from the Greek for messenger
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A bell is carried across the ocean to the States by a courier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion and the church bell rung morning, noon and evening to call people to it.

clue.text: From long line rushes to show insincere grief

blocks.note: a crocodile is a long line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
tears means rushes, as in tears down the road

explanation.surface: Someone at the end of a long queue rushes off, putting on a show of sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the legend that crocodiles weep while eating prey, so it means faked sorrow.
